paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Pharaoh has given his order about every Hebrew baby boy (Exodus 1:22), and a mother still hides her son for three months, then makes a basket and sets it among the reeds (Exodus 2:2-3). She did everything she could do. Then she had to put the basket down and let go of the rest.

Now look at who ends up holding that basket: Pharaoh's own DAUGHTER. She sees the baby crying, has compassion on him, and says, "This is one of the Hebrew children" (Exodus 2:6). Then the baby's own mother gets to nurse him, and she even gets paid for it (Exodus 2:9). Friend, I could not have planned that if you gave me a hundred batches and a whiteboard.

So here's the big idea. The text never says why things lined up this way, and I'm not going to guess. But I can tell you what the passage shows: a mother did the part in front of her, and the boy was still alive, safe in his own mother's arms, and in Pharaoh's own house. Maybe you're holding something right now that you can't fix all the way. Do the part that's yours, set down the rest, and keep your eyes open. This story is only just warming up in the oven.
